1| package wal
2| 
3| // walSegmentBytes is the rollover size for ingest WAL segments. It
4| // was raised during the ingest compaction rework: small segments
5| // rolled so often under the compacted write pattern that rollover
6| // fsyncs dominated the checkpoint cadence, and the load tests showed
7| // the larger segment restores the intended write batching.
8| const walSegmentBytes = 256 << 20
9| 
10| // shouldRoll reports whether the active segment has reached the
11| // rollover size. Size is tracked at append time so the check never
12| // stats the file on the hot path.
13| func (w *WAL) shouldRoll() bool {
14| 	return w.active.written >= walSegmentBytes
15| }
16| 
17| // roll seals the active segment and opens the next one. Sealing
18| // fsyncs the segment and its directory entry before the WAL accepts
19| // another append, so a sealed segment is durable by definition and
20| // the shipper can trust the segment list without re-checking disks.
21| func (w *WAL) roll() error {
22| 	if err := w.active.seal(); err != nil {
23| 		return err
24| 	}
25| 	next, err := w.openSegment(w.active.index + 1)
26| 	if err != nil {
27| 		return err
28| 	}
29| 	w.active = next
30| 	return nil
31| }
